summary.text: A 20-year-old nulliparous professional bowler presented with lower abdominal pain and had no notable past medical, surgical or family history. Examination showed a soft, non-tender abdomen and a mobile, enlarged lower abdominal mass. Ultrasonography and MRI showed a unilocular cyst of the left ovary; CA 19-9 was mildly elevated and other tumor markers were within normal ranges.

The preoperative diagnosis was serous cystadenoma of the left ovary, and vNOTES ovarian cystectomy under general anesthesia was completed without complications in 66 minutes with minimal blood loss; histopathology confirmed a benign serous cystadenoma.

She had minimal postoperative pain, walked independently on postoperative day one, was discharged on day three, resumed training on day four with only mild discomfort, was completely asymptomatic by day 10, and competed in a national tournament on day 23, placing fourth. Long-term follow-up data were not available.
